# What every test returns

<small>Source: [`man/test_results.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/test_results.Rd) · Help: `?test_results`</small>

Every exported `perform*Test()` function returns a base-R `htest` object, so a result prints, subsets and composes like the result of `stats::t.test()` or `lmtest::bptest()`. This page lists every field such a result can hold: the five every test returns, the two optional `htest` fields some return, and the fields a few tests add. `tests/testthat/test-return-contract.R` checks every exported test against it.

## Fields of every test

`statistic`
:   the test statistic: a numeric value of length one, named after the statistic (`"X-squared"`, `"F"`, `"t"`, `"GQ"`, `"LM"`, `"z"`, ...).

`parameter`
:   the parameters of the null distribution: a numeric vector whose elements are named, usually degrees of freedom (`"df"`, or `"df1"` and `"df2"`). The resampling tests store the number of replications here (`"B"`, `"permutations"`), and the tests on ordered observations the sizes they use (`"n"`, `"m"`). It is `NULL` for [`performPesaranTest()`](performPesaranTest.md), whose statistic is referred to the standard normal distribution.

`p.value`
:   the p-value: a single number between 0 and 1.

`method`
:   a character string naming the test. When an argument switches between two statistics, such as `studentize` in [`performHarveyTest()`](performHarveyTest.md), the string says which one was computed.

`data.name`
:   a character string describing what was tested: the formula of the model, followed for some tests by the variance regressors. For [`performBoxMTest()`](performBoxMTest.md), which tests data rather than a model, it names the data and the grouping.

## Optional htest fields

`alternative`
:   a character string describing the alternative hypothesis, returned by the tests that have a direction or a stated alternative.

`estimate`
:   estimates that accompany the statistic: a named numeric vector ([`performSzroeterTest()`](performSzroeterTest.md), [`performSpearmanTest()`](performSpearmanTest.md), [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md)), or, in [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md), a matrix of slope estimates with one column per quantile and named rows and columns.

## Fields some tests add

`p.value_bootstrap`
:   [`performWhiteTestRobust()`](performWhiteTestRobust.md) and [`performBPTestRobust()`](performBPTestRobust.md) with `bootstrap = TRUE`: the bootstrap p-value.

`robust_details`
:   [`performWhiteTestRobust()`](performWhiteTestRobust.md) and [`performBPTestRobust()`](performBPTestRobust.md): a list with the confidence interval, effect size, bootstrap results, power and sample size, and `method` or `studentized`, the setting that chose the statistic.

`boot_statistics`
:   [`performWhiteTestBootstrap()`](performWhiteTestBootstrap.md): the bootstrap replicates of the statistic.

`bootstrap`
:   [`performWildBootstrapTest()`](performWildBootstrapTest.md): a list with the replicates, the number of usable ones, the multiplier distribution and the observed statistic.

`permutation`
:   [`performRankPermutationTest()`](performRankPermutationTest.md): a list with the replicates, the number of usable ones and the ordering variable.

`projection`
:   [`performHighDimensionalTest()`](performHighDimensionalTest.md): a list with the number of principal components kept, the share of the variance they explain and the threshold that chose them.

`variance_function`
:   [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md): a list with the form of the variance function, its regressors and the added terms that were tested.

`quantiles`, `se_type`, `iid`
:   [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md): the quantiles compared and the settings of the standard errors.

`chunks_processed`, `chunk_size`, `r_squared`
:   [`performWhiteTestStreaming()`](performWhiteTestStreaming.md), [`performBPTestStreaming()`](performBPTestStreaming.md) and [`performKoenkerTestStreaming()`](performKoenkerTestStreaming.md): how the data were read and the \(R^2\) of the auxiliary regression.

`res`
:   [`performSpatialHeteroTest()`](performSpatialHeteroTest.md): the Monte Carlo replicates of Moran's I from `spdep::moran.mc()`, whose class `"mc.sim"` the result keeps.

## Attributes

[`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md) and [`performWhiteTestRobust()`](performWhiteTestRobust.md) attach the attributes `auxiliary_regressors`, `original_regressors`, `cross_products_included` and `r_squared_auxiliary`, which describe the auxiliary regression. [`runHeteroTests()`](runHeteroTests.md) adds attributes of its own to each result it returns.

## Inputs every test refuses

Since 0.15.0 every test on a model refuses four inputs, each with one message: a `glm` that is not a least-squares
fit, that is, of any family but `gaussian` or with any link but the identity ("needs a model fitted by
stats::lm()"); a model with a coefficient that is not finite, infinite, `NaN`, or `NA` without the fit being
rank-deficient ("Model coefficients must be finite"); `data` that lack rows the model was fitted to; and
`data` that lack a variable of the model ("The following variables are missing from"). Until 0.16.0 the
`NA` of an aliased term was refused too; since then a rank-deficient fit is tested on the estimable part of its
design (see *Supported models*). The model frame is accepted as `data` as it is. A `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link is accepted by every `perform*Test()` function and gives the result of the `lm` up
to rounding error, when the two decide the rank of the design alike (see *Supported models*);
[`performWhiteTestStreaming()`](performWhiteTestStreaming.md), [`performHarrisonMcCabeTest()`](performHarrisonMcCabeTest.md) and
[`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md) refused every `glm` until 0.16.0, and [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md)
until 0.17.0, which bootstraps it as the `lm` it is. With positive prior weights it gives the result of
`lm(..., weights = w)`: [`performGQTest()`](performGQTest.md), [`performRESETTest()`](performRESETTest.md),
[`performWhiteTestBootstrap()`](performWhiteTestBootstrap.md), [`performWildBootstrapTest()`](performWildBootstrapTest.md) and
[`performHarrisonMcCabeTest()`](performHarrisonMcCabeTest.md), which read the weights of an
`lm`, read the prior weights of the `glm`, and [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md), which refuses
a weighted `lm`, and [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md), which refuses weights that did not come from
[`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md), refuse it with the same message. With a zero prior weight it is refused as the `lm` with a
zero weight is ("The model was fitted with zero or non-finite weights"), since 0.16.0. A `survey::svyglm()` fit is
refused by every test ("The model is a `survey::svyglm()` fit"). `tests/testthat/test-input-validation.R`
gives every test these inputs. Since 0.17.0 a `MASS::rlm()` fit is refused by every test too, with class
`heteroTests_model_context_error` (see *Supported models*), which `tests/testthat/test-model-context.R`
checks.

The tests that read `data` also refuse `data` whose rows cannot be confirmed to hold the observations of
the fit ("cannot match the rows of `data` to the observations of the model"). They match the rows of `data`
to the residuals by row name, and a tibble, a data.table or a data frame whose row names were reset, as by
`dplyr::arrange()`, has row names that only number its rows. Before a test reads `data`, the rows the row
names pick are compared with the model frame of the fit, row by row: every column `data` holds under its own
name, value by value, and the others (`log(x)`, `poly(x, 2)`, `offset(o)`, the weights and an offset
given as arguments) computed from `data` as the fit computed them. A term computed from the rows it is given,
such as `I(x - mean(x))`, and a column that names a variable `data` does not hold, are not compared; for a
term of variables of `data`, the compared columns must then tell the rows of the fit apart. Data that cannot be
confirmed so are refused, even the data of the fit: when no column can be compared, as with `lm(d$y ~ d$x)`, or
when the compared columns tie on rows that differ in such a term. Pass the full data the model was fitted on, or the
variables as columns of `data`. Data without row names of their own in another order
than the fit, or with rows in
front of those of the fit, are refused, as are repeated row names, and a model frame rebuilt for a fit with
`model = FALSE` from data that changed after the fit. Data with row names of their own are matched by name, in
any order; until 0.16.0 [`performPesaranTest()`](performPesaranTest.md), [`performBPRandomEffectsTest()`](performBPRandomEffectsTest.md) and
[`performScatterDiagnostic()`](performScatterDiagnostic.md) read `data` by position, and refused such data in another order than
the fit. `tests/testthat/test-data-alignment-guard.R` checks these refusals.

Since 0.16.0 [`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md), [`performBPTest()`](performBPTest.md), [`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md),
their streaming forms, [`performWhiteTestStreaming()`](performWhiteTestStreaming.md), [`performBPTestStreaming()`](performBPTestStreaming.md) and
[`performKoenkerTestStreaming()`](performKoenkerTestStreaming.md), which read the design of the fit chunk by chunk where each chunk built
its own from the rows of `data`, [`performRankPermutationTest()`](performRankPermutationTest.md), [`performHighDimensionalTest()`](performHighDimensionalTest.md), the studentized
Breusch-Pagan statistic ([`performStudentizedBPTest()`](performStudentizedBPTest.md), [`performBPTestRobust()`](performBPTestRobust.md) with
`studentize = TRUE`, the registered `"student_bp"`), [`performRESETTest()`](performRESETTest.md),
[`performGQTest()`](performGQTest.md), [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md), [`performGlejserTest()`](performGlejserTest.md),
[`performParkTest()`](performParkTest.md), [`performSzroeterTest()`](performSzroeterTest.md) with the registered `"szroeter"`,
[`performHarrisonMcCabeTest()`](performHarrisonMcCabeTest.md), [`performHartleyFmaxTest()`](performHartleyFmaxTest.md),
[`performSpatialHeteroTest()`](performSpatialHeteroTest.md), the five group tests, [`performLeveneTest()`](performLeveneTest.md),
[`performBrownForsytheTest()`](performBrownForsytheTest.md), [`performFlignerKilleenTest()`](performFlignerKilleenTest.md),
[`performBartlettTest()`](performBartlettTest.md) and [`performOBrienTest()`](performOBrienTest.md), the two panel tests,
[`performPesaranTest()`](performPesaranTest.md) and [`performBPRandomEffectsTest()`](performBPRandomEffectsTest.md), and so
[`runPanelTests()`](runPanelTests.md), and [`performScatterDiagnostic()`](performScatterDiagnostic.md), and the tests computed from the model
alone, [`performSpearmanTest()`](performSpearmanTest.md), [`performHarveyTest()`](performHarveyTest.md), [`performArchLMTest()`](performArchLMTest.md),
[`performMcLeodLiTest()`](performMcLeodLiTest.md), [`performCookWeisbergTest()`](performCookWeisbergTest.md) and [`performNCVTest()`](performNCVTest.md),
[`performSpreadLevelTest()`](performSpreadLevelTest.md), [`performDavidianCarrollTest()`](performDavidianCarrollTest.md) and
[`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md), with [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md), read the response, the design, the
residuals, the weights and the offset from the fit, through the model context of the package, and read from
`data` only the rows the comparison above confirmed; the other tests follow in later steps (the design page of
the site, <https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/heteroTests/design/model-context/>, sets out the plan). RESET, the
tests computed from the model alone and `fitWLS()` without `var_formula` read nothing from `data`,
and match it as the other tests do, so that every test takes and refuses the same data; until 0.16.0 they gave the
value of the fit on numbered data in another order, rows in front of those of the fit and repeated row names, and
refused numbered data in the order of the fit whose row numbers are not the fit's (`fitWLS()` ignored
`data`). A second formula, the `var_formula` of the Cook-Weisberg test, of the
variance form test and of `fitWLS()`, and the `against` of the variance form test, is evaluated on the
confirmed rows of `data`, or, without `data`, on the model frame; a variable that neither holds is refused,
where it was found in the workspace.
The Goldfeld-Quandt, Szroeter and Harrison-McCabe tests read their `order_by`, Glejser's and Park's their
`variable` and Hartley's and the group tests their `group` from the confirmed rows of `data`, or,
without `data`, from the model frame when it holds the variable under its own name ("The following variables
are missing from the model frame of `model`" otherwise). Hartley's test refuses a group that is missing at an
observation of the fit; the group tests leave such observations out, with the warning "Removed N observations due
to missing values in ...", as before 0.16.0. The panel tests read their `id` and `time`, and the scatter
diagnostic its `vars`, from the confirmed rows of `data`; without `data` the panel tests read them from
the model frame, when it holds them under their own names, and the scatter diagnostic needs `data`. Pesaran's
test refuses a pair of `id` and `time` that holds two observations of the fit and a unit or a period
missing at an observation of the fit, and computes the statistic of an unbalanced panel, whose units are not all
observed at the same periods, from the periods each pair of units shares, as `plm::pcdtest()` does. The registered `"szroeter"` orders by the fitted values, which it computes
from the fit, and the spatial test reads no column of `data`: its `listw` lists the observations of the
fit in its order. Harrison-McCabe takes the rank of the fit, decided at the fit's tolerance (`1e-7` for an
`lm`, `1e-11` for a `glm`). These tests
match numbered rows by the row numbers of the fit, or, when `data` holds one row per observation and its numbers
are not those of the fit, in the order of the fit, once those rows reproduce the model frame; they drop nothing
before the match, so data that hold the rows a fit with `na.omit` dropped, or only the rows it kept, numbered
again, are accepted. Since 0.17.0 a fit with `na.action = na.exclude` is tested as the same fit with
`na.omit`, which drops the same rows, with the same values, refusals and warnings: before, the tests refused it
("Model residuals must be finite"), RESET stopped on it ("NA/NaN/Inf in 'x'"), and the panel tests and the scatter
diagnostic read its residuals, padded with `NA` at the rows it dropped, against the rows of `data` by
position, which gave a statistic that was `NA`, or computed with the `NA`. An output with one value per row,
as the estimated variances `fitWLS()` attaches to its fit, is padded with `NA` at the rows the fit dropped,
as `residuals()` and `weights()` of such a fit are. Named data in any order, numbered data in the order of the fit: numbered data in another order
are refused, as by the other tests. They need no `data` for a model that transforms its variables, has an
`offset()` term, or takes its weights or offset from a column of the data, and accept its model frame as
`data`. They also refuse a multivariate `lm` ("needs a model with one response"), a fit whose coefficients,
residuals or weights were changed after it was fitted ("does not reproduce its residuals from its design and
coefficients", "The weights of the model are not those its coefficients were fitted with"), a fit whose terms do
not rebuild the design of its coefficients, as a `fitWLS()` fit of an `mgcv::gam()` fit with smooth terms
(the first of these messages, since 0.17.0), and a fit with
`model = FALSE` whose model frame can no longer be rebuilt, unless `data` gives its response and fitted
values, on which it is then tested. The tests that fit the model again by least squares, or whose null
distribution is derived for the least-squares residuals of its design, refuse an `mgcv::gam()` fit with
penalised smooth terms, which is not the least-squares fit of its design, and the others test it on that design,
the basis of its smooths, since 0.17.0 (see *Supported models* below). The
residuals of a `gam` carry no names, and these tests match `data` to its observations by the row names of
its model frame; the tests that are not built on the context yet and read a column of `data` match them by
position. The check of an edited fit is a guard against accidental edits, not a proof
that a fit is unedited: an edited coefficient leaves the residuals unchanged, so it is seen only at `1e-7` of
the largest term of the response, the design times the coefficients and the residuals, and an edit of 0.5 goes
undetected once the response is above about `1e7`. These refusals have class `heteroTests_model_context_error`, which
[`runHeteroTests()`](runHeteroTests.md) and [`runDiagnostics()`](runDiagnostics.md) keep, as they keep that of a refusal of
`data`, without running another test under the name of the one refused; since 0.17.0 a grouped run stops
with such a refusal in a group too, where the group recorded it as a failed test of `NA`. A test that reads a column of
`data` the model frame does not hold, as the rank permutation, Goldfeld-Quandt, Szroeter and
Harrison-McCabe tests do with their `order_by`, Glejser's and Park's with their `variable`, Hartley's
and the group tests with their `group`, the panel tests with their `id` and `time` and the scatter
diagnostic with its `vars`, refuses numbered rows taken in the order of the fit if two rows of the
fit tie on every
compared column. On a call with more than one defect, the first one
reported may differ from before 0.16.0, since the rows of `data` are now matched before the checks of the model.
`tests/testthat/test-model-context.R` checks them.

## Supported models

The tests examine the residuals of a least-squares fit for a variance that is not constant, so they accept the models
whose residuals are those of a least-squares fit, and refuse the others early, with the messages above. Which test
accepts which class, measured by running every test on each, is the table of the *Supported models* page of the
documentation site; `tests/testthat/test-model-eligibility.R` and `test-input-validation.R` check it.

- An `lm` is accepted by every test.
- An `lm(..., weights = w)` is accepted: `lm()` states that the error variance is \(\sigma^2 / w_i\), and the tests read the Pearson residuals \(\sqrt{w_i}\, e_i\), which have constant variance when the weights are right. [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md), which refits without them, refuses it, and [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md) refuses weights that did not come from [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md).
- A zero weight: the observation is not part of the fit, and its residual is an artificial zero that a test would count. Refused by every test but [`performRESETTest()`](performRESETTest.md), an F test of two nested weighted least-squares fits, in which a zero weight drops the observation from both; it gives the value of the fit to the observations with positive weight. Keeping that exception was decided on 2026-10-17.
- An offset, given as `offset = o` or as an `offset()` term: the residuals of the fit include it, and the tests that read them account for it. Four left it out of a refit and returned a value that was not that of the model; they refused it in the development of 0.16.0 (decided 2026-10-17), and since the offset fix of 0.16.0 they read the offset from the fit and carry it in every refit: [`performGQTest()`](performGQTest.md), [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md) and the studentized Breusch-Pagan statistic ([`performStudentizedBPTest()`](performStudentizedBPTest.md), [`performBPTestRobust()`](performBPTestRobust.md) with `studentize = TRUE`, the registered `"student_bp"`) give the value of the model fitted to the response minus the offset, and [`performRESETTest()`](performRESETTest.md) the nested F test of the model with its offset against the model augmented with the powers of its fitted values, \(X\hat\beta + o\) (decided 2026-10-18).
- A `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link is a least-squares fit. With prior weights \(w_i\) it is fitted by maximum likelihood, which for normal errors of variance \(\phi / w_i\) maximises \(-\sum_i w_i (y_i - x_i^\top \beta)^2 / (2\phi)\): weighted least squares. Iteratively reweighted least squares, the algorithm of `glm()`, then has the working response \(y_i\) and the working weights \(w_i\) whatever the current estimate, so its first step reaches the solution of `lm(..., weights = w)` (Nelder and Wedderburn, 1972; McCullagh and Nelder, 1989, sections 2.5 and 3.6). It is Fisher scoring, and for the identity link, the canonical link of the Gaussian family, the information does not depend on \(y\), so scoring is Newton-Raphson, which converges in one step when the log-likelihood is quadratic in \(\beta\) (Green, 1984, section 1.2). Its design, coefficients, fitted values, residuals and weights are those of the `lm`, up to rounding, so a test whose statistic and null distribution are functions of those, under the assumptions of the linear model, which the `glm` states, gives the result of the `lm`: every `perform*Test()` function does, weighted or not (`tests/testthat/test-input-validation.R` and `test-model-eligibility.R` compare them). That holds when the two decide the rank of the design alike: `lm()` aliases a column with the tolerance `1e-7` of its QR decomposition, `glm.fit()` with `min(1e-7, epsilon / 1000)`, `1e-11` by default, so on a column within that margin of a combination of the others, such as `x3 = x1 + 1e-9 * rnorm(n)`, the `glm` keeps it and gets the values of `lm(..., tol = 1e-11)`, not those of the default `lm`. [`performWhiteTestStreaming()`](performWhiteTestStreaming.md), [`performHarrisonMcCabeTest()`](performHarrisonMcCabeTest.md) and [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md) refused every `glm` until 0.16.0, and [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md) refits it as that `lm` since then. [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md) refused every `glm` until 0.17.0, as it refits each replicate by least squares, which would drop a family and a link; it bootstraps a Gaussian `glm` with the identity link as that `lm`, with its prior weights, and refuses any other `glm`, as before. It refused every `mgcv::gam()` fit until 0.17.0, and refuses one with penalised smooth terms since then (see the item on the `gam` below). The checks of the model read its R-squared, which `summary()` of a `glm` does not report, as that of the `lm`: `summary.lm()` applied to the `glm`, whose fitted values, residuals, weights and offset are those of the `lm`, so that a near-perfect fit is refused as the `lm` is, since 0.16.0. The *Supported models* page of the documentation site sets out the argument; the references are below, and the section numbers of McCullagh and Nelder (1989) are those of its table of contents. The tests read its prior weights, `model$prior.weights`, and never `model$weights`, which holds the working weights of the last iteration of iteratively reweighted least squares, \(w_i (d\mu_i/d\eta_i)^2 / V(\mu_i)\). For this family and link the two are equal up to rounding; for any other they depend on the fitted means. A `glm` fitted with weights that are all 1 has the `prior.weights` of one fitted without weights, so the tests take it for an unweighted fit, where `lm(..., weights = rep(1, n))` is a weighted one: [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md) and [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md), which refuse a weighted fit, accept the `glm` and refuse the `lm`.
- Any other `glm`, such as a binomial or a Poisson one, is refused: its residuals have a variance that depends on the mean by construction, so a test of constant variance tests nothing the help pages describe.
- A `survey::svyglm()` fit is refused: its residuals are scaled by the sampling weights, which are not precision weights. See [`runSurveyHeteroTests()`](runSurveyHeteroTests.md).
- Panel models: [`performPesaranTest()`](performPesaranTest.md) and [`performBPRandomEffectsTest()`](performBPRandomEffectsTest.md), and so [`runPanelTests()`](runPanelTests.md), take a pooled `lm` and the columns of `data` that name the units and the periods. A `plm::plm()` fit is not an `lm`: every test refuses it, as it refuses anything but an `lm` or a `glm`, with one message, which names the class received and points to the pooled `lm()`.
- A rank-deficient fit: a term that is a linear combination of others, or the dummy of a cell of an interaction that no observation falls in, leaves an `NA` coefficient. Its residuals and fitted values are the projection on the column space of the design, which the aliased columns do not change. Since 0.16.0 every test that accepts the model without the aliased columns accepts it, computed on the estimable part of the design: the columns that were not aliased, with degrees of freedom from the rank, so that it gives the statistic and p-value of the model fitted without them. A test that refuses that model refuses the rank-deficient one with the same message. The model without them is the one `lm()` keeps: its decomposition keeps a column unless it is a combination of the columns before it, so of an aliased set the column that comes last, in the order of the terms, is left out. Most statistics depend only on the space the columns span, and are the same whichever column is left out. Two depend on which: [`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md), and its robust, streaming and bootstrap forms, when the cross products are left out (`cross_products = FALSE`, `method = "reduced"`, or more regressors than `max_interactions`), as the squares are those of the columns kept; and [`performHighDimensionalTest()`](performHighDimensionalTest.md) when it keeps fewer principal components than columns. With `form = "power"`, [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md) takes the logarithms of every column of the design, the aliased ones included, so its value is not that of the model without them (and does not depend on the order of the terms); with the exponential form, the default, it is.
- A `fitWLS()` fit is a weighted `lm`, with estimated weights: accepted, but the reference distributions take the weights as known ([`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md) accounts for the estimation).
- A `MASS::rlm()` fit, such as [`fitRobust()`](fitRobust.md) returns, is an `lm` by class and an M-estimate, whose residuals are not least-squares residuals. Since 0.17.0 every test refuses it, with an error of class `heteroTests_model_context_error` that names the `lm()` fit of the same formula to test instead, and so do [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md), the registered names and the runners, which keep the refusal final. Until then 37 tests took it for an `lm` and tested its M-estimation residuals as if they were least-squares ones, the studentized Breusch-Pagan statistic tested the least-squares refit of its design, and [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md) and [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md) refused it as a weighted fit, its case weights, all 1 unless given, being read as precision weights.
- An `mgcv::gam()` fit with the Gaussian family and the identity link, a `glm` by class, is tested on its stored design, `model.matrix()`: its parametric columns and the basis of its smooths. A smooth term is penalised unless it is fixed, `s(x, fx = TRUE)`, and the residuals of a penalised fit are not those of the least-squares fit of that design. Since 0.17.0 the tests that read only its residuals, its fitted values, columns of `data` and the columns of the design as auxiliary regressors test a penalised fit, the streaming tests on the basis too, as the exact tests do, where they read the variables of the formula. The tests that fit it again by least squares, or whose null distribution is derived for the least-squares residuals of its design, refuse it with class `heteroTests_model_context_error`, and the runners keep the refusal final: [`performGQTest()`](performGQTest.md), [`performRESETTest()`](performRESETTest.md), [`performQuantileRegressionTest()`](performQuantileRegressionTest.md), the studentized Breusch-Pagan statistic, [`performWhiteTestBootstrap()`](performWhiteTestBootstrap.md), [`performWildBootstrapTest()`](performWildBootstrapTest.md), [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md) and the robust forms with `bootstrap = TRUE`, [`performVarianceFormTest()`](performVarianceFormTest.md) and [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md), which refitted it without its penalty, and [`performHarrisonMcCabeTest()`](performHarrisonMcCabeTest.md) and [`performSzroeterTest()`](performSzroeterTest.md), which compared its residuals with the null distribution of least-squares ones. A `gam` that is the least-squares fit of its design, without smooth terms or with fixed ones, is tested by every test as the `lm()` of that design, the refitting and resampling tests included, where the fixed smooths were refused as penalised ones. Whether a `gam` is that fit is decided from the fit: its design refitted by least squares, with its weights and offset, gives its residuals to `1e-8` of the largest residual of that refit, plus `1e3` times the machine epsilon of the largest value of the response and of the offset, the rounding of a fit on that scale, so that an offset or a trend of any size does not change the verdict. A `gam` without a penalised term that fails the check is refused as one whose residuals are not those of that fit, not as a penalised one. Decisions 37 and 38 of the design of the model context (decided on 2026-10-29) set this out.

[`checkModel()`](checkModel.md) checks the class of a model only, `lm` or `glm`; it does not check whether a test
accepts it.
